problems.title: A trigonometric quotient of two differences
problems.question: Evaluate $(\sin35^\circ\sin84^\circ-\sin55^\circ\sin6^\circ)/(\cos50^\circ\sin21^\circ-\cos40^\circ\cos21^\circ)$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
steps: The numerator is $\sin(35^\circ-6^\circ)=\sin29^\circ$.
The denominator is $-\cos(40^\circ+21^\circ)=-\cos61^\circ=-\sin29^\circ$, nonzero. The ratio is $-1$.

problems.title: A quadratic inequality in cosine
problems.question: Solve $2\cos^2x+5\cos x+2\ge0$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
steps: Since $t+2>0$ throughout the cosine range, require $t\ge-1/2$.
The cosine inequality gives intervals from $-2\pi/3$ to $2\pi/3$, repeated every $2\pi$.

problems.title: A sine-square substitution with a quadrant restriction
problems.question: Find $\cot x$ if $6\sin^4x+\sin^2x=1$ and $\pi<x<3\pi/2$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
steps: $6t^2+t-1=(3t-1)(2t+1)=0$ gives $t=1/3$. In quadrant III, both sine and cosine are negative.
Thus $\sin x=-1/\sqrt3$, $\cos x=-\sqrt{2/3}$ and $\cot x=\sqrt2$.

problems.title: Surface area of a regular triangular pyramid
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has apothem 6 cm and base dihedral angle $60^\circ$. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
formulas: Base inradius $\rho=l\cos\beta$; equilateral side $s=2\sqrt3\rho$; lateral area $=Pl/2$.
steps: $\rho=6\cos60^\circ=3$, so the base side is $6\sqrt3$. Its area is $s^2\sqrt3/4=27\sqrt3$.
Base perimeter is $18\sqrt3$, giving lateral area $(18\sqrt3)(6)/2=54\sqrt3$. Total is $81\sqrt3$.

problems.title: Area of a rhombus from distances to its plane and sides
problems.question: A point is distance 12 from the plane of rhombus $ABCD$ and 13 from each side. If $AB+CD=30$, find its area.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
formulas: Projected distance to each side $r=\sqrt{13^2-12^2}$; tangential-polygon area $=rP/2$.
steps: The projection is equidistant from both pairs of parallel sides, hence is the rhombus centre. Its distance to each side is 5.
Each side is 15, so perimeter is 60 and area $5\cdot60/2=150$.

problems.title: A radical times a sine equals zero
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{25-4x^2}\sin(2\pi x)=0$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
formulas: Domain $|x|\le5/2$; a product is zero when either factor is zero.
steps: The radical vanishes at $x=\pm5/2$. The sine vanishes for $x=k/2$, $k\in\mathbb Z$.
Within the domain, $k=-5,-4,\ldots,5$; this already includes the radical endpoints.

problems.title: A diagonal section of a square-pyramid frustum
problems.question: A regular square-pyramid frustum has base sides $4\sqrt2,3\sqrt2$ and height 4. Find section area $A_1B_1CD$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
formulas: The section is a trapezoid; distance between its parallel bases is $\sqrt{h^2+((a+b)/2)^2}$.
steps: The top edge $A_1B_1$ lies opposite bottom edge $CD$. Their horizontal separation is $(4\sqrt2+3\sqrt2)/2=7\sqrt2/2$.
The section altitude is $\sqrt{16+49/2}=9/\sqrt2$. Multiply it by the mean base length $7\sqrt2/2$.

problems.title: A trigonometric system and parity of periods
problems.question: Solve $\tan x+\tan y=2$, $\cos x\cos y=1/2$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
formulas: $\sin(x+y)=(\tan x+\tan y)\cos x\cos y$; sine is at most 1.
steps: The first relation yields $\sin(x+y)=1$, hence $\cos(x+y)=0$. Since $\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y$, the sine product is also $1/2$.
Thus $\tan x\tan y=1$. Two real numbers with sum 2 and product 1 are both 1, so $x=\pi/4+m\pi,y=\pi/4+n\pi$.
The cosine product is $(-1)^{m+n}/2$, so the final condition is that $m+n$ is even.

problems.title: A prism height depends on which leg is named
problems.question: A right triangular prism has base right angle $C$, legs 3 and 4, and plane $ACB_1$ makes $45^\circ$ with the base. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
steps: The base area is 6 and perimeter 12. A section perpendicular to hinge $AC$ gives $h=BC$.
If $BC=4$, height is 4 and total area $12+48=60$. If $BC=3$, height is 3 and total area $12+36=48$.
problems.note: The printed problem gives the two leg lengths without assigning either to AC or BC. Both label assignments satisfy its stated data, so both total areas must be retained.

problems.title: An inverse-trigonometric equation
problems.question: Solve $2\arcsin(2x)=\arccos(7x)$.
problems.idea: Reduce the expression or geometry to a standard identity, preserving the domain.
steps: The right side is nonnegative, so $x\ge0$. On $[0,1/7]$ the left side lies in $[0,\pi]$, where cosine is injective.
Take cosine: $1-8x^2=7x$, or $(8x-1)(x+1)=0$. Only $x=1/8$ is in the domain and has the required sign.
